cases.title: is true when the provider has at least one managed account
cases.reason: A managed account is enough to keep its provider usage section renderable.

cases.title: is true with zero managed accounts when active rate-limit data exists (system default)
cases.reason: System-default credentials with real windows render despite zero managed accounts.

cases.title: is false with zero accounts and no usable rate-limit data
cases.reason: No accounts plus no usable data hides the provider usage section.

cases.title: returns inactive usage using the runtime rateLimits payload shape
cases.reason: Inactive usage is found through the actual runtime rateLimits payload shape.

cases.title: is null when there are no limits or the window has no reset timestamp
cases.reason: Absent limits, absent windows and absent reset timestamps omit the reset label.

cases.title: formats minutes, hours+minutes, and days+hours like the desktop tooltip
cases.reason: Independent minute/hour/day examples verify the displayed reset countdown.

cases.title: formats exact hours and exact days without a zero remainder
cases.reason: Exact hour/day boundaries omit a zero remainder in displayed countdowns.

cases.title: reports "Resets now" for a reset timestamp in the past
cases.reason: Past reset timestamps produce Resets now rather than negative time.

cases.title: reads the requested window only
cases.reason: Requesting an absent weekly window cannot read the populated session window.

cases.title: keeps stale window data visible during a transient error
cases.reason: Cached window data remains visible during a transient provider error.

cases.title: shows loading for a fetching provider without a window
cases.reason: A fetching provider without its requested window shows loading rather than unavailable.

rationale: Retain the actual nested wire decoder, forward fields, old-host defaults and meaningful malformed payload rejection.

cases.title: validates nested account/rate-limit state and preserves forward-compatible fields
cases.reason: Independent extension fields survive nested schema decoding for forward compatibility.

cases.title: defaults missing runtime targets for older host-only snapshots
cases.reason: Older host-only snapshots default omitted runtime targets safely.

cases.title: rejects malformed %s
cases.reason: Each table-driven nested mutation reaches the real decoder and rejects invalid account/runtime/limit/credit data.

cases.title: rejects a host target that smuggles a WSL distro
cases.reason: A host runtime carrying a WSL distro is rejected as an inconsistent scope.

rationale: Retain meaningful rendered monitoring/error states and native animation scheduling; both status components execute their production effect logic.

cases.title: renders a static Activity heartbeat for a monitoring agent
cases.reason: A monitoring agent renders its static heartbeat without scheduling a working animation.

cases.title: renders a static Activity heartbeat for an all-monitoring workspace
cases.reason: A monitoring workspace also renders a static heartbeat without scheduling a working animation.

cases.title: keeps the spinner fallback when workingMode is absent
cases.reason: Older host rows without workingMode retain their working spinner fallback.

cases.title: keeps both native working rings off the interaction queue
cases.reason: Both native working animations use the native driver without holding the interaction queue.

cases.title: draws %s with its own dot colour
cases.reason: User-interrupted agents remain muted while failed agents use the error color.

rationale: Retain the web-only repair control and native-app recovery direction; remove a separate test that pins an unchanged generic sentence.

cases.title: offers Re-pair alone, and its press reaches the screen
cases.reason: The actual web banner exposes only Re-pair and pressing it calls repair alone.

cases.title: names the app for reconnect and removal, not for re-pair
cases.reason: Users are told that reconnect and removal must happen in the app.

cases.title: keeps the sentence that says what happened
cases.reason: Exact generic authentication prose is copied from the component without exercising recovery; the retained cases check actionable guidance and routing.

rationale: Consolidate native action inventory into routing, and check each named action independently so swapped callbacks cannot pass aggregate totals.

cases.title: offers Retry, Re-pair and Remove
cases.reason: The retained routing case already mounts these controls and now asserts the same displayed action set.

cases.title: routes each press to the action the screen gave it
cases.reason: Press each named control with counters reset and assert only its intended callback; pressing all then checking one of each masked handler permutations.

cases.title: drops Retry alone when there is no host to retry against
cases.reason: Without a retryable host, Retry disappears while repair and removal remain.

rationale: Retain actual animation callback ownership: a Back press during hiding must not restart/cancel the animation and strand a native modal.

cases.title: still closes an open drawer on Android Back
cases.reason: Back on an open drawer reaches onClose once after completing its animation.

cases.title: lets the hide finish when Back is pressed mid-close
cases.reason: Back mid-hide leaves the original animation able to fire onHidden without another close request.

rationale: Retain actual wrapper state transitions, latest callback ownership and late-hide behavior across reopening.

cases.title: keeps close stable and delivers the latest action once after unmount
cases.reason: A stable hide callback unmounts before delivering the latest close action exactly once despite duplicate completion.

cases.title: a hide that lands after a reopen does not swallow the next close
cases.reason: A hide completion delivered after reopening cannot latch the next legitimate close.

rationale: Retain externally visible sheet geometry at keyboard and tiny-viewport boundaries; explicit inputs give independent space expectations.

cases.title: fills the space under the safe top when the keyboard is closed
cases.reason: Without a keyboard, the sheet fits beneath the safe top and explicit gap.

cases.title: shrinks by the keyboard inset so the sheet top stays under the status bar
cases.reason: A keyboard inset shrinks the available sheet height rather than overlapping the input area.

cases.title: never expands past the space above the keyboard on tiny viewports
cases.reason: A small viewport permits a 34px sheet rather than enforcing a minimum that overlaps system chrome.

rationale: Retain iOS/Android keyboard-frame distinctions and negative inset clamping, which affect actual keyboard docking.

cases.title: uses the full keyboard frame for fill sheets on iOS and Android
cases.reason: Fill-mode drawers use the true keyboard top on both platforms.

cases.title: subtracts the home-indicator inset only for iOS content-sized sheets
cases.reason: Content-sized iOS sheets subtract the home-indicator portion already covered by padding.

cases.title: uses the full IME height for Android content-sized sheets
cases.reason: Android IME height excludes its navigation bar, so content sheets retain the full inset.

cases.title: never returns a negative inset
cases.reason: A short keyboard frame relative to safe-bottom padding clamps to zero.

rationale: Retain actual layered-drawer/native-modal integration, terminal close cleanup and Back ownership.

cases.title: opens a sheet over another inside the one native Modal
cases.reason: Opening a form over an issue detail renders both in exactly one native Modal.

cases.title: keeps the Modal through the last close animation, then leaves none to swallow taps
cases.reason: The last closing animation retains its Modal until completion, then removes it so taps are not intercepted.

cases.title: hands Back to the sheet on top, then to the one under it
cases.reason: Back first closes the top form and after its removal reaches the underlying detail sheet.

rationale: Retain the small closing-state predicate because its remaining RightDrawer caller must mount immediately and keep exit animation content alive.

cases.title: mounts before opening and stays mounted while closing
cases.reason: The explicit visibility/mounted matrix preserves opening and closing content, including false-visible/true-mounted exit state.

rationale: Retain enter-transform and real content-mount observations when nested pickers hand the native window back.

cases.title: re-asserts the enter transform when a pinned sheet takes the window back
cases.reason: Reacquiring interactivity schedules a fresh enter transform for the pinned sheet.

cases.title: rebuilds the sheet subtree when it takes the window back
cases.reason: A handback mounts fresh content, detecting the native-view repair that shared-value writes alone cannot prove.

cases.title: does not re-assert or rebuild while the sheet stays pinned
cases.reason: A sheet staying pinned neither re-enters nor rebuilds its content on unrelated updates.

rationale: Retain the negotiated host compatibility contract and actual hook cleanup; fold malformed-list schema coverage into the public capability reader.

cases.title: enables reset only when the host explicitly advertises the contract
cases.reason: An explicitly advertised reset contract enables the real capability reader through status.get.

cases.title: fails closed for an unsupported or malformed host response
cases.reason: Retain unsupported/malformed cases and add missing/mixed-type lists through the real reader, replacing direct schema-only acceptance assertions.

cases.title: fails closed when the capability probe cannot complete
cases.reason: A rejected capability request fails closed rather than leaking a reset action.

cases.title: uses the reconnect-safe probe and cancels it on unmount
cases.reason: The mounted hook publishes a supported result from the reconnect-safe probe and cancels on unmount.

rationale: Remove redundant direct schema tests; the public reader now covers whole-list salvage, while actual reset requests already exercise scope and snapshot decoding.

cases.title: drops a capability list carrying a non-string, whole, as main did
cases.reason: Move missing/mixed-type capability list coverage into readCodexResetCreditCapability so it observes the actual disabled-action decision.

cases.title: forwards the redeem reply whole to decodeResetResult
cases.reason: Two accepted values merely restate z.unknown(); they do not prove forwarding to decodeResetResult despite the title. Real request tests already validate decoded outcomes and rejection.

rationale: Retain real scope generation and request/response handling for a scarce credit; mocked RPC responses are decoded and compared against independent account/runtime expectations.

cases.title: hides the action when no earned credit is available
cases.reason: Without an available earned credit, no reset summary/action is offered.

cases.title: formats singular and plural availability with the next expiry
cases.reason: Singular/plural availability and independent expiry durations produce the intended visible summary.

cases.title: binds a host offer to the exact managed active account and revision
cases.reason: A host offer binds account identity, account revision and a versioned offer.

cases.title: binds a WSL offer only to the exact distro selection and account
cases.reason: A WSL offer binds the selected distro and excludes another configured distro account.

cases.title: fails closed for system-default, unknown WSL distro, and account/target mismatch
cases.reason: System-default, unknown distro and mismatched account/runtime selections produce no spendable scope.

cases.title: maps %s to user-facing copy
cases.reason: Each actual reset outcome maps to a distinct useful user message.

cases.title: sends a fresh key and the exact scope with a 90s timeout, and keeps nothing on the phone
cases.reason: The request sends the exact confirmed scope, a fresh UUID and timeout, then decodes the returned snapshot.

cases.title: mints a new key per attempt, as the desktop does, leaving retries to the host ledger
cases.reason: A failed transport attempt and retry use different keys while decoding an already-redeemed host result.

cases.title: accepts the account unresolved attempt the host resumes when the retry names a newer offer
cases.reason: A newer offer retry can accept an unresolved same-account attempt bound to the old offer.

cases.title: returns a definite stale-offer rejection for the screen to re-confirm
cases.reason: A definite stale-offer refusal is decoded for a fresh user confirmation.

cases.title: rejects a mismatched scope or a malformed nested snapshot
cases.reason: Mismatched account/revision and malformed nested snapshots are rejected through the real request path.

cases.title: rejects a valid snapshot that does not describe the returned redeemed scope
cases.reason: A structurally valid snapshot describing the wrong active account cannot validate a redeemed scope.

rationale: Retain actual modal/storage integration and write serialization; the fake storage controls refusal/delay but production generates the stored list and mirror update.

cases.title: does not let the refusal escape as an unhandled rejection
cases.reason: An actual Add press catches persistence refusal, keeps the modal open and leaves callbacks/mirror unchanged.

cases.title: reports the key and closes when the store takes it, so the case above is the refusal
cases.reason: The same Add flow reports success and closes after accepted persistence, providing a real positive control.

cases.title: rejects when the store refuses, so a caller never drops the row
cases.reason: A refused remove rejects so the caller cannot discard a row not removed from storage.

cases.title: answers the stored list without the key once the store takes it
cases.reason: An accepted remove returns the actual retained stored list.

cases.title: lets two removals in flight together both land
cases.reason: Two concurrent removals preserve both updates in stored data.

cases.title: removes from the list a settings save in flight stored, not the list before it
cases.reason: A removal queued behind a settings reorder reads the newly written list and preserves its order.

cases.title: writes nothing when the stored list cannot be read, so a read failure erases nothing
cases.reason: A storage read failure prevents any destructive write based on invented empty state.

cases.title: writes nothing and keeps the drawer open
cases.reason: The actual modal stays open and writes nothing when Add cannot read prior stored keys.

cases.title: an add replaces %s with the new key
cases.reason: Each malformed stored value can be replaced by an actual new key through the modal Add flow.

cases.title: a removal replaces %s with an empty list
cases.reason: Removing from malformed stored values writes an explicit empty key list.

cases.title: loading %s shows no keys
cases.reason: Loading malformed stored values safely exposes no keys.

rationale: Retain independent public worklet-algorithm examples; the component suite uses two rows, whereas these verify multi-row intermediate shifts and boundary inputs.

cases.title: round-trips keys through positions
cases.reason: Converting nonnumeric keys to positions and ordering them restores the caller order.

cases.title: clamps drag indexes to the list bounds
cases.reason: Negative, in-range, past-end and empty-list indexes obey list bounds.

cases.title: shifts intermediate rows down when dragging a row later
cases.reason: A later four-row move shifts only the intermediate rows and preserves the outside row.

cases.title: shifts intermediate rows up when dragging a row earlier
cases.reason: An earlier four-row move shifts only the intermediate rows and preserves the outside row.

cases.title: returns the same positions for no-op or unknown moves
cases.reason: Unknown and no-op moves preserve the original positions reference.

rationale: Retain actual parser/serializer outcomes for link removal while preserving artifact structure; these are distinct from browser paint/navigation checks.

cases.title: leaves no element a browser would treat as a link
cases.reason: Rewritten output reparses without active anchor or area hrefs.

cases.title: inerts a fragment link too, because a fragment is not a scroll in this frame
cases.reason: Fragment and empty links lose navigation attributes while keeping their text and destination heading.

cases.title: keeps the text, the headings and the images the author wrote
cases.reason: Author text, heading/image data, title and anchor order survive the inerting pass.

cases.title: drops the target with the href, so no non-link carries link markup
cases.reason: Rewritten anchors lose target as well as href so stale link markup is not retained.

cases.title: reaches an image map and an SVG link, which a pass over `a[href]` alone would not
cases.reason: Image-map and SVG link forms are reached while unrelated area geometry survives.

cases.title: leaves an anchor that was never a link alone, which is most of what a document has
cases.reason: An existing name-only anchor keeps its identifier.

cases.title: keeps the doctype whole, identifiers and all
cases.reason: Public/system doctype identifiers survive serialization and absent doctypes are not invented.

cases.title: writes back the leading newline the serialiser owes each preformatted block
cases.reason: Preformatted block leading newlines receive the serializer compensation without prefixing normal text.

cases.title: does not run or fetch what the artifact carries, because nothing here has a context
cases.reason: Parsing script markup leaves it inert and retains its source rather than running it.

cases.title: leaves an href inside a comment where a regex pass would have found it
cases.reason: An href inside a comment stays literal while a real neighboring anchor is rewritten.

cases.title: reaches a link inside a declarative shadow root, and inside one nested in it
cases.reason: Nested declarative-shadow-root templates are traversed and lose links at every depth.

rationale: Retain real preview component wiring from shell grant to inert document, sandbox and source toggle.

cases.title: hands the artifact over untouched when the shell can open a link
cases.reason: A shell that can open links receives the original document and navigation-capable sandbox.

cases.title: hands over an artifact with no link, in a frame that cannot navigate, when it cannot
cases.reason: Without the grant, the actual frame receives inert links while preserving artifact text and IDs.

cases.title: seals the frame with a sandbox that grants nothing, rather than dropping the attribute
cases.reason: The refused frame gets an explicitly empty sandbox attribute rather than an absent unrestricted one.

cases.title: takes the frame away when Source is showing, on either answer
cases.reason: Activating Source removes the iframe for either grant answer and mounts the source view.

rationale: Remove private boolean/constant checks duplicated by existing rendered Android/iOS selection and long-press coverage.

cases.title: keeps inline selection everywhere but Android
cases.reason: A three-string truth table restates the private platform condition; existing real Markdown tests prove Android transcript selection and iOS range selection behavior.

cases.title: resolves the running platform once
cases.reason: Asserting the imported constant is false under a mocked Android flag adds no rendered selection evidence; the actual Android prose/long-press suite already runs that policy.
